title: Dietary plant polysaccharides as modulators of brain aging: mechanistic links to inflammaging, the gut brain axis and amyloid tau pathology.
abstract: Objectives: This review critically evaluates chemically characterized plant-derived polysaccharides (PS) as dietary modulators of brain aging, focusing on their structural features, gut-brain mechanisms and effects on neuroinflammation, amyloid pathology and tau-related pathways. Methods: Molecular, in vitro, preclinical and early human studies were critically examined. Evidence was assessed in relation to PS molecular weight, branching, charge, monosaccharide composition, purity, fermentability, dosage and associated non-carbohydrate constituents. Particular attention was given to gut microbiota modulation, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production, barrier integrity, immune signaling, microglial activation and neurodegenerative biomarkers. Results: Fermentable plant PS altered gut microbial composition and increased acetate, propionate and butyrate production in experimental models. These SCFAs may influence brain aging through FFAR2/FFAR3 signaling and histone deacetylase inhibition, thereby improving intestinal barrier function, regulating peripheral inflammation and modifying microglial responses. Direct anti-amyloid effects were supported mainly by in vitro studies, whereas evidence for tau modulation remained indirect and predominantly preclinical. Animal studies provided the strongest causal support, particularly through microbiota-transfer, antibiotic-depletion and receptor-pathway experiments. Human evidence was limited to associative studies and small fiber or prebiotic trials. Reported PS molecular masses ranged from about 10 kDa to more than 1,000 kDa, with preclinical doses of 50-500 mg/kg and human intakes of 5-15 g/day. Discussion: Plant PS are promising dietary modulators of brain aging but not established neurotherapeutics. Translation requires standardized fractions, control of co-extracted phenolics and proteins, dose-response studies and biomarker-rich clinical trials incorporating stool and plasma SCFAs, inflammatory markers, neurofilament light, phosphorylated tau, cognitive outcomes and neuroimaging measures.
screening_reason: The review examines the links between dietary polysaccharides, gut microbiota modulation, the gut-brain axis, and neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、植物由来多糖類（PS）が腸・脳軸、神経炎症、アミロイドおよびタウ病理に及ぼす影響と、脳老化修飾因子としての可能性を評価しています。発酵性植物多糖類は腸内細菌叢の組成を変化させ、短鎖脂肪酸（SCFA）の産生を増加させることが実験モデルで示されています。これらのSCFAは、腸管バリア機能の改善や末梢炎症の制御、ミクログリア応答の修飾を通じて脳老化に影響を与える可能性があります。しかし、直接的な抗アミロイド効果は主に試験管内研究に留まり、タウ修飾に関する証拠も間接的かつ前臨床段階のものです。
summary_en: This review evaluates plant-derived polysaccharides as dietary modulators of brain aging, focusing on their gut-brain mechanisms and neuroinflammatory pathways. Fermentable polysaccharides increase short-chain fatty acid production in experimental models, potentially regulating microglial responses and peripheral inflammation. However, direct anti-amyloid and tau-modulating effects remain largely limited to in vitro and preclinical studies.
key_finding_ja: 植物由来多糖類は腸内細菌叢を介した短鎖脂肪酸産生を促進し、脳老化や神経炎症を修飾する可能性が示されているが、その直接的な治療効果の証拠は主に前臨床段階に留まっている。
why_it_matters_ja: 食事性多糖類による脳老化抑制の臨床応用には、標準化された画分の使用や、便・血漿中のバイオマーカーを用いた厳密な臨床試験による検証が求められる。

title: Clinical applications of gut microbiome for non-invasive diagnosis of colorectal neoplasia.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common malignancy and the second leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. While screening programs have reduced mortality, current stool-based tests such as the faecal immunochemical test (FIT) and tumour marker assays, remain limited in sensitivity for adenoma detection and rely on relatively later-stage biological signals in the carcinogenic process. False positives lead to unnecessary invasive procedures, whilst missed adenomas continue to progress, highlighting the need for alternative strategies. Accumulating evidence implicates the gut microbiome in CRC pathogenesis, which involves tumour-associated dysbiosis and microbial ecosystem shifts. Multinational metagenomic studies have consistently identified reproducible microbial signatures that can serve as biomarkers of disease and may predate the biological signals used in conventional screening. PCR-based microbial markers have emerged as practical tools for clinical application, enabling sensitive and specific detection of adenomas and CRC. A recent microbial panel incorporating Fusobacterium nucleatum, Hungatella hathewayi, Christensenella hongkongensis, and a novel bacterial gene marker m3 from Lachnoclostridium demonstrated improved sensitivity for adenomas whilst maintaining comparable accuracy for CRC. International guidelines have begun to recommend combining microbiome-based assays with FIT into integrated screening programs that target multiple biologic processes across the pathogenesis. Microbiome-based stool testing represents a promising non-invasive approach that improves detection of adenomas in early-stage disease, often missed by FIT alone and could enable more refined risk stratification. Further validation across diverse populations, assessment of cost-effectiveness, and integration into established screening infrastructures will be critical for broad clinical adoption.
authors: Cui C, Shi H, Naito Y, Otani K, Chan FKL.
screening_reason: The paper focuses on the clinical applications of the gut microbiome and microbial signatures for diagnosing colorectal neoplasia.
summary_ja: 大腸がん（CRC）のスクリーニングにおいて、便潜血化学検査（FIT）などの既存の検査法は腺腫検出の感度が低いという課題があります。近年のメタゲノム研究により、大腸がんの病態に関与する再現性の高い腸内細菌叢シグネチャーが同定され、バイオマーカーとしての活用が期待されています。特に、Fusobacterium nucleatumやLachnoclostridium由来の新規遺伝子マーカーなどを組み合わせた細菌パネルは、腺腫に対する検出感度を向上させることが示されています。腸内細菌叢ベースの検査とFITを組み合わせた統合的スクリーニングは、早期発見を改善する有望な非侵襲的アプローチとして注目されています。
summary_en: Conventional stool-based tests for colorectal cancer screening have limited sensitivity for detecting early-stage adenomas. Recent metagenomic studies have identified reproducible gut microbial signatures that can serve as non-invasive biomarkers for early detection. Combining microbiome-based assays with conventional tests like FIT represents a promising strategy to improve adenoma detection and risk stratification.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢の特定の細菌や遺伝子マーカーを組み合わせたパネル検査は、従来の便潜血検査単独よりも大腸腺腫の検出感度を向上させることが示されている。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢を利用した非侵襲的スクリーニングが確立されれば、大腸がんの早期発見率が向上し、不要な侵襲的検査を減らせる可能性があるが、多様な集団での検証が必要である。

title: Forsythiae Fructus attenuates DSS-induced colitis and associated neuroinflammation with modulation of AMPK/mTOR-related autophagy signaling.
abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Forsythiae Fructus, the dried fruit of Forsythia suspensa (Thunb.) Vahl is a traditional herbal medicine widely used in East Asia for inflammatory disorders. Although Forsythiae Fructus exhibits anti-inflammatory activity in experimental colitis, its effects on colitis-associated brain inflammation and autophagy-related signaling remain unclear. Aim of the study This study investigated the protective effects of Forsythiae Fructus extract (FF) on intestinal and brain inflammatory responses in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis mice and explored the involvement of AMPK/mTOR-related signaling. Materials and methods Mice received FF (100 mg/kg) or 5-aminosalicylic acid (ASA, 100 mg/kg) by oral gavage once daily for 15 days. DSS (5%, w/v) was administered in drinking water from day 7 to day 12, followed by a 3-day recovery period with normal drinking water (day 12-15). Disease severity, intestinal permeability, inflammatory mediators, and autophagy-related markers in the colon and brain were assessed using endoscopy, histology, ELISA, immunoblotting, immunofluorescence, and RT-qPCR. Results FF substantially alleviated DSS-induced colitis by attenuating body weight loss (-9.0% vs. -17.1% in DSS), reducing the disease activity index by approximately 40%, increasing colon length by 18%, and decreasing intestinal permeability by approximately 59%. FF restored epithelial barrier integrity by increasing Occludin, ZO-1, Muc2, and Tff3 expression. It also decreased IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α levels in the colon, serum, and brain, accompanied by reduced microglial activation and NF-κB signaling. FF increased AMPK phosphorylation and LC3B-II/LC3B-I ratios while reducing mTOR activation and SQSTM1 accumulation in both colon and brain tissues. Conclusions FF effectively alleviated DSS-induced colitis, reducing disease activity by approximately 40% and restoring intestinal barrier function. These protective effects were accompanied by suppression of intestinal and brain inflammatory responses and modulation of AMPK/mTOR-related autophagy signaling. These findings provide experimental support for the traditional use of FF in inflammatory disorders and highlight its potential as a protective candidate for ulcerative colitis and its associated gut-brain inflammatory manifestations.
authors: Park YJ, Pak ME, Yang HJ, Jin HJ, Kim KY, Hwang YH, Li W, Go Y.
screening_reason: The study investigates the attenuation of colitis and associated neuroinflammation, focusing on gut-brain inflammatory manifestations.
summary_ja: 東アジアで炎症性疾患に用いられる伝統生薬である連翹（Forsythiae Fructus）の、大腸炎およびそれに伴う脳内炎症（神経炎症）に対する効果をマウスモデルで検証しました。デキストラン硫酸ナトリウム（DSS）誘発大腸炎マウスにおいて、連翹抽出物の経口投与は体重減少や大腸の短縮を抑制し、腸管バリア機能を回復させました。さらに、連翹は大腸、血清、および脳における炎症性サイトカインのレベルを低下させ、ミクログリアの活性化を抑制しました。これらの保護効果には、大腸および脳組織におけるAMPK/mTORを介したオートファジーシグナル伝達の調節が関与していることが示されました。
summary_en: This study investigated the protective effects of Forsythiae Fructus extract (FF) on intestinal and brain inflammatory responses in DSS-induced colitis mice. Oral administration of FF alleviated colitis severity, restored epithelial barrier integrity, and reduced inflammatory cytokines in the colon, serum, and brain. These protective effects were accompanied by the suppression of microglial activation and the modulation of AMPK/mTOR-related autophagy signaling.
key_finding_ja: 連翹抽出物は、DSS誘発大腸炎マウスにおいて腸管バリア機能を回復させるとともに、AMPK/mTORシグナル調節を介して大腸および脳の炎症反応（神経炎症）を抑制する。
why_it_matters_ja: 本研究は、連翹が潰瘍性大腸炎およびそれに伴う腸・脳相関の炎症性病態に対する新たな治療候補となる可能性を実験的に示している。

title: Evolution of the fecal and oral microbiota after prophylactic antibiotics administered for dental surgeries.
abstract: Background The human oral and gut microbiomes play critical roles in maintaining overall health. Although systemic antibiotics are frequently prescribed perioperatively in dental procedures, their impact on microbiota composition and diversity remains inadequately understood. The authors' objective was to characterize the evolution of the gut and oral microbiomes after a course of antibiotics administered for dental surgeries. The authors hypothesized that the microbiome would experience disruption but eventually recover to baseline levels and that patient-related factors would influence the extent of disruption and recovery. Methods Saliva and stool samples were collected from patients undergoing dental surgeries and receiving prophylactic antibiotics (n = 64) at baseline and then at 3, 10, 30, and 90 days after surgery. Microbial diversity and composition were assessed using 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing. Shotgun metagenomics sequencing was applied to a subset of samples to evaluate changes in antimicrobial resistance genes. Results Significant (P Conclusions The findings highlight the dynamic response of the human microbiome to antibiotic exposure and oral surgery and underscore the importance of antibiotic stewardship in practice. Further research on functional outcomes and host-microbiome interactions is warranted to optimize perioperative care in dentistry. Practical implications Consideration of patient factors is essential to minimize unnecessary disruption of the microbiome and mitigate the risk of developing resistance.
authors: Littlejohn C, Chang YC, Teles F, Korostoff JM, Redding LE.
journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
screening_reason: The study characterizes the evolution and disruption of the human gut microbiome following antibiotic administration.
summary_ja: 歯科手術において予防的抗菌薬が頻繁に処方されますが、口腔および腸内細菌叢への影響は十分に解明されていません。本研究では、歯科手術に伴い予防的抗菌薬を投与された患者64名を対象に、術前および術後3、10、30、90日目の唾液と糞便サンプルを解析しました。その結果、抗菌薬投与後に微生物の多様性と組成に有意な変化が観察され、一部の患者では術後90日目でもベースラインへの完全な回復が見られませんでした。また、ショットガンメタゲノミクス解析により、抗菌薬耐性遺伝子のプロファイルにも変化が生じることが示されました。
summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of prophylactic antibiotics on the oral and gut microbiomes of 64 patients undergoing dental surgeries. Significant disruptions in microbial diversity and composition were observed after antibiotic administration, with some patients failing to fully recover to baseline by day 90. Shotgun metagenomics also revealed alterations in antimicrobial resistance gene profiles following treatment.
key_finding_ja: 歯科手術時の予防的抗菌薬投与は、口腔および腸内細菌叢の多様性と組成に有意な破壊を引き起こし、一部の患者では術後90日を経過しても完全には回復しない。
why_it_matters_ja: 歯科領域における不必要な抗菌薬処方を減らし、耐性菌リスクを抑制するためには、患者個別の要因を考慮した適切な抗菌薬適正使用（スチュワードシップ）が重要である。

title: Cannabinoid receptor-mediated modulation of the gut-brain axis under chronic stress: Neuroinflammatory mechanisms, microbial metabolites, and sexual dimorphism.
abstract: Chronic stress disrupts the gut-brain axis (GBA) through coordinated dysfunction of the intestinal barrier and of the vascular interfaces that protect the brain, fostering a neuroinflammatory state implicated in mood disorders, neuropsychiatric conditions, and chronic pain. This narrative review synthesizes evidence across five domains. First, the inflammatory cascade by which stress-induced disruption of the epithelial and gut vascular barriers activates the NLRP3 inflammasome and sustains central neuroinflammation. Second, microbial metabolites, namely short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan-kynurenine products, and indole derivatives, as modulators of gut-brain homeostasis. Third, the gut microbiome-endocannabinoidome axis, including the capacity of commensal bacteria to generate endocannabinoid-like N-acyl amides that engage host receptors. Fourth, the receptor-specific pharmacology of phytocannabinoids, distinguishing Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), which acts principally at CB1 and CB2 with comparable affinity, from cannabidiol (CBD), which has low affinity for these receptors and signals mainly through TRPV1, TRPA1, GPR55, PPARs, and 5-HT1A. Fifth, sexual dimorphism in barrier vulnerability and treatment response. In rodent models, chronic stress reduces intestinal and blood-brain barrier tight junction expression, elevates circulating lipopolysaccharide, and activates the NLRP3 inflammasome, while tryptophan metabolism shifts toward neurotoxic kynurenine products. Cannabinoid modulation of the kynurenine pathway and cannabinoid-mediated restoration of blood-brain barrier integrity remain mechanistic hypotheses extrapolated from indirect evidence rather than demonstrated mechanisms in chronic psychological stress paradigms. Human data are largely limited to small trials of microbiota-targeted interventions and of CBD in anxiety, and to observational endocannabinoidome-microbiome studies. These observations provide a preclinical rationale for GBA-targeted pharmacological strategies, with translational claims explicitly separated from mechanistic plausibility.
authors: Neves LBM, Domingues D, Baldessarini BL, Laino P, Lima BC.
screening_reason: The review focuses on the gut-brain axis, neuroinflammatory mechanisms, and gut microbiome-endocannabinoidome interactions under stress.
summary_ja: 本ナラティブレビューは、慢性ストレス下における腸・脳軸（GBA）の破綻と神経炎症のメカニズムについて、5つの領域から証拠を統合しています。ストレスによる上皮および腸血管関門の破壊がNLRP3インフラマソームを活性化し、中枢神経炎症を持続させる機序を説明しています。また、短鎖脂肪酸などの微生物代謝物、腸内細菌叢-エンドカンナビノイドシステム軸、フィトカンナビノイドの受容体特異的作用、およびバリアの脆弱性における性差について議論しています。ただし、カンナビノイドによるキヌレニン経路の修飾や血液脳関門の回復は、慢性心理ストレスモデルにおいて実証されたものではなく、間接的な証拠に基づく仮説段階に留まっています。
summary_en: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on how chronic stress disrupts the gut-brain axis and promotes neuroinflammation through epithelial and vascular barrier dysfunction. It highlights the roles of microbial metabolites, the endocannabinoidome, phytocannabinoid pharmacology, and sexual dimorphism in barrier vulnerability. The review notes that many cannabinoid-mediated mechanisms remain hypothetical extrapolations rather than demonstrated pathways in chronic psychological stress.
key_finding_ja: 慢性ストレスによる腸・脳軸の破綻と神経炎症の機序において、微生物代謝物やカンナビノイド受容体を介した修飾作用が注目されているものの、多くの治療的機序は依然として間接的な証拠に基づく仮説段階に留まっている。
why_it_matters_ja: カンナビノイドを用いた腸・脳軸標的治療の臨床応用に向けては、動物モデルでの仮説とヒトでの実証データを明確に区別し、さらなる検証を進める必要がある。

title: Astrovirus infection alters gut microbial communities in a widespread neotropical bat across human-modified landscapes.
abstract: Astroviruses are becoming a growing concern in public and veterinary health. In humans, astrovirus infections can cause severe diarrhea and may lead to neuropathological encephalitis, whereas in wildlife, these enteropathogenic viral infections often lack overt symptoms and thus remain unnoticed. Yet their close interaction with the host's gastrointestinal microbiome might drive cascading effects with disadvantages for host health. Bats harbor many zoonotic viruses without showing signs of disease, and many species move freely along the gradient from pristine to agricultural landscapes. To better understand the impact of astrovirus (AstV) infection under a One Health framework, we investigated the gut microbiome of naturally AstV-infected Seba's short-tailed bats (Carollia perspicillata, n = 234) inhabiting old-growth lowland forests or forest fragments embedded in an agricultural matrix in Panama. AstV prevalence was higher in forest fragments. We observed that AstV infection is associated with a shift in microbial beta but not alpha diversity, which points towards the replacement of common gut microbial taxa when infected. Indeed, potentially beneficial bacteria, such as Lactococcus, decreased in abundance, whereas potentially pathogenic bacteria from the Helicobacter genus increased in AstV-positive bats. Two Helicobacter haplotypes closely related to avian Helicobacter species were identified. We conclude that even though the impact of infection on the microbiome was not amplified in forest fragments, the higher infection likelihood in landscapes altered by humans implies more frequent or prolonged health repercussions for bats.
authors: Brändel SD, Melville DW, Wilhelm K, Corman VM, Page R, Drosten C, Tschapka M, Sommer S, Wasimuddin.
screening_reason: The paper directly examines the impact of viral infection on the gut microbiome and microbial communities of bats.
summary_ja: アストロウイルス（AstV）感染は野生動物において不顕性であることが多いが、宿主の腸内細菌叢との相互作用が健康に影響を及ぼす可能性がある。本研究では、パナマの原生林および断片化した森林に生息するコウモリ（Carollia perspicillata、n = 234）を対象に、自然AstV感染が腸内細菌叢に与える影響を調査した。AstV感染率は人間活動により改変された森林断片で高く、感染は腸内細菌叢のβ多様性の変化と関連していた。具体的には、感染個体においてLactococcus属などの有益な細菌が減少し、Helicobacter属などの潜在的な病原性細菌が増加していた。
summary_en: This study investigated the impact of natural astrovirus (AstV) infection on the gut microbiome of Seba's short-tailed bats in Panama across different landscapes. AstV prevalence was higher in forest fragments, and infection was associated with significant shifts in microbial beta diversity. In AstV-positive bats, the abundance of potentially beneficial Lactococcus decreased, while potentially pathogenic Helicobacter increased. These findings suggest that habitat fragmentation and viral infection interact to alter the gut microbial communities of wildlife.
key_finding_ja: コウモリにおけるアストロウイルス感染が、有益な乳酸菌の減少と潜在的病原体であるヘリコバクター属の増加を伴う腸内細菌叢の組成変化を引き起こすことを明らかにした。
why_it_matters_ja: 人為的に改変された環境における野生動物のウイルス感染と腸内細菌叢の乱れとの関連性を示したことは、ワンヘルス（One Health）の観点から野生動物の健康維持や人獣共通感染症のリスク評価において重要です。

title: Exosome-mediated delivery of 3-n-butylphthalide rescues microglial energy crisis and ameliorates neuroinflammation in ischemic stroke.
abstract: Stroke remains the second leading cause of death and the primary cause of long-term disability worldwide, with ischemic stroke accounting for the majority of cases. Ischemia triggers robust microglial activation, yet the precise regulatory mechanisms underlying microglial functional reprogramming remain incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that excessive mitophagy drives metabolic energy failure in microglia following cerebral ischemia, resulting in impaired phagocytosis and exacerbated neuroinflammation. Analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing data from mouse brains in the sham, transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO, mMCAO), and permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pMCAO, sMCAO) groups revealed that mitophagy was markedly activated in microglia under sustained ischemia and was associated with impaired phagocytic and cytoskeletal pathways. In vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) assays showed that phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons by microglia induced upregulation of Drp1, triggering excessive mitochondrial fission and mitophagy, which caused ATP depletion and reduced clearance capacity. The mitophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine alleviated inflammatory responses but failed to restore mitochondrial quality. In contrast, 3-n-butylphthalide (NBP) stabilized mitochondrial membrane potential, restored ATP production, and improved microglial phagocytic defects and inflammation. To achieve targeted delivery, we constructed BV2 microglia-derived exosomes encapsulating NBP (BV2 exo @ NBP), which efficiently enhanced drug accumulation in ischemic lesions and significantly improved neurological outcomes in stroked mice. These results identify excessive mitophagy as a core mechanism underlying microglial energy crisis after cerebral ischemia and provide a mitochondria-targeted therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke. Importantly, the neuroprotective efficacy, mitochondrial restoration, and anti-inflammatory effects of BM@NEB were fully recapitulated in 18-month-old aged mice, a clinically relevant model that more closely reflects the stroke patient population, supporting the translational potential of this exosome-based therapeutic strategy.
authors: Wang B, Xi M, Lin K, Guo Q, Wang Y.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
screening_reason: The paper investigates a therapeutic strategy to ameliorate microglial activation and neuroinflammation in ischemic stroke.
summary_ja: 脳虚血後において、過剰なマイトファジーがミクログリアの代謝エネルギー不全を引き起こし、貪食能の低下と神経炎症の悪化を招くことが示されました。3-n-ブチルフタリド（NBP）は、ミクログリアのミトコンドリア膜電位を安定化させ、ATP産生を回復させることで、貪食不全と炎症を改善しました。さらに、NBPを内包したBV2ミクログリア由来のエクソソーム（BV2 exo @ NBP）を構築し、虚血病変への標的デリバリーを実現しました。このエクソソーム製剤は、若齢および高齢の脳梗塞マウスモデルにおいて、神経学的転帰を顕著に改善しました。
summary_en: This study demonstrates that excessive mitophagy drives metabolic energy failure and impairs phagocytosis in microglia following cerebral ischemia, leading to exacerbated neuroinflammation. Treatment with 3-n-butylphthalide (NBP) stabilized mitochondrial membrane potential, restored ATP production, and improved microglial phagocytic defects. To enhance delivery, BV2 microglia-derived exosomes encapsulating NBP were developed, which successfully accumulated in ischemic lesions and improved neurological outcomes in both young and aged stroke mouse models.
key_finding_ja: 脳虚血後のミクログリアにおける過剰なマイトファジーがエネルギー危機の核心的なメカニズムであることを同定し、NBP内包エクソソームによるミトコンドリア標的治療が神経炎症を軽減し神経学的転帰を改善することを示しました。
why_it_matters_ja: 臨床現場の患者集団をより反映した高齢マウスモデルでも有効性が確認されたことから、脳梗塞に対する新たなエクソソームベースの治療戦略としてのトランスレーショナルな可能性が期待されます。

title: Effects of Araticum ( Annona crassiflora Mart.) By-Product on Intestinal Health Parameters in High-Fat Diet-Fed Mice.
abstract: Obesity is a major public health issue associated with metabolic disturbances and alteration in the gut microbiota. Studies indicate that bioactive compounds can modulate these processes, and fruit by-products represent a promising source of such compounds. This study investigated the impact of araticum ( Annona crassiflora Mart.) by-product on intestinal microbiota composition and obesity biomarkers in mice fed a high-fat diet. The by-product was characterized for technological and proximate composition. Forty-six Swiss mice were randomized into four groups: a control diet group, a high-fat diet group, a high-fat diet + araticum by-product (200 mg kg-1) group, and a high-fat diet + araticum by-product (400 mg kg-1) group. After 30 days, murinometric, biochemical, and histological parameters and the composition of microbiota were assessed. The by-product contained 8.04 g.100 g-1 of moisture, 11.17 g.100 g-1 of protein, 9.79 g.100 g-1 of lipids, 53.29 g.100 g-1 of total fiber (3.96 g.100 g-1 soluble and 49.33 g.100 g-1 insoluble), 2.97 g.100 g-1 of ash, and 14.74 g.100 g-1 of digestible carbohydrates. Araticum by-product consumption did not affect weight gain or glucose tolerance but increased fecal moisture content and reduced pH. Regarding gut microbiota composition, the supplemented groups showed a trend toward a higher relative abundance of Firmicutes. In the group receiving the highest dose of araticum by-product (400 mg kg -1 ), more intense intestinal PAS staining was observed, which may indicate a greater presence of PAS-positive mucin-containing structures. These preliminary findings suggest that the araticum by-product may influence selected intestinal parameters, although its functional effects require confirmation in longer-term and mechanistic studies.
authors: de Souza TR, de Oliveira FL, Neves Casarotti S, de França Lemes SA, Pereira Avila ET, Sabino Damazo A, de Carvalho LAL, Guariz Pinheiro D, Sivieri K, Caldeira Morzelle M.
screening_reason: The study investigates the impact of a dietary by-product on intestinal microbiota composition in mice.
summary_ja: 高脂肪食を摂取させたマウスを対象に、アラティクム（Annona crassiflora Mart.）副産物が腸内細菌叢および肥満バイオマーカーに及ぼす影響を30日間にわたり調査しました。アラティクム副産物の摂取は、体重増加や糖耐性には影響を与えませんでしたが、糞便の水分量を増加させ、pHを低下させました。腸内細菌叢においては、添加群でFirmicutes門の相対存在量が増加する傾向がみられました。また、高用量（400 mg/kg）投与群では腸管のPAS染色性が高まり、ムチン含有構造の増加が示唆されました。
summary_en: This study investigated the effects of an araticum (Annona crassiflora Mart.) by-product on intestinal health and microbiota in mice fed a high-fat diet. While the supplementation did not alter weight gain or glucose tolerance, it increased fecal moisture, reduced fecal pH, and showed a trend toward a higher relative abundance of Firmicutes. Additionally, the highest dose of the by-product increased intestinal PAS staining, suggesting a potential increase in mucin-containing structures.
key_finding_ja: 高脂肪食マウスへのアラティクム副産物の投与は、体重や糖耐性には影響しなかったものの、糞便pHの低下やFirmicutes門の増加傾向、腸管ムチン含有構造の増加を示唆する変化をもたらしました。
why_it_matters_ja: 果物加工副産物が腸内環境や粘膜バリア機能に影響を与える可能性を示しており、機能性食品素材としての有効性を検証する今後の長期的な研究の基礎となります。

title: Development of Recombinant Anti-TLR2 Antibodies and PLGA Nanoparticle-Based Gene Therapy for the Treatment of Neuropathic Pain.
abstract: Neuroinflammation is a key contributor to neuropathic pain, with microglial Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) playing a central role in initiating and sustaining proinflammatory responses. However, existing TLR2-targeting antibodies are limited by poor delivery to the central nervous system and short-lived efficacy. We developed a non-viral gene therapy strategy using biodegradable poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles (NPs) to deliver recombinant anti-TLR2 antibody genes. High-affinity nanobody and single-chain variable fragment candidates were selected through phage display screening and shown to suppress TLR2-dependent signaling both in vitro and in vivo. In mouse models of neuropathic pain, a single intrathecal administration of PLGA NP-encapsulated antibody genes produced robust and sustained analgesia, accompanied by reduced glial activation and proinflammatory cytokine expression. These findings demonstrate a modular NP-based platform for sustained antibody expression in the central nervous system and establish its potential for the treatment of chronic pain driven by innate immune activation.
authors: Lee S, Jeon J, Lee H, Barcelon EE, Hong J, Lee SJ.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
screening_reason: The study investigates a gene therapy targeting microglial TLR2 to suppress neuroinflammation and neuropathic pain.
summary_ja: 神経障害性疼痛における神経炎症を抑制するため、抗TLR2抗体遺伝子を封入した生分解性PLGAナノ粒子を用いた非ウイルス性遺伝子治療法が開発されました。スクリーニングにより選定された抗体遺伝子は、in vitroおよびin vivoにおいてTLR2依存性シグナルを抑制しました。神経障害性疼痛のマウスモデルへの単回クモ膜下腔内投与により、持続的な鎮痛効果が得られ、グリア細胞の活性化と炎症性サイトカインの発現が抑制されました。このナノ粒子プラットフォームは、中枢神経系における持続的な抗体発現を可能にし、慢性疼痛の治療に寄与する可能性があります。
summary_en: Researchers developed a non-viral gene therapy using PLGA nanoparticles to deliver recombinant anti-TLR2 antibody genes for treating neuropathic pain. In mouse models, a single intrathecal administration of these nanoparticles achieved sustained analgesia and suppressed glial activation and proinflammatory cytokine expression. This modular platform offers a potential strategy for long-term antibody delivery to the central nervous system to treat chronic pain driven by innate immune activation.
key_finding_ja: 抗TLR2抗体遺伝子を搭載したPLGAナノ粒子の単回クモ膜下腔内投与により、マウスモデルにおいてグリア活性化の抑制を伴う持続的な鎮痛効果が示されました。
why_it_matters_ja: 中枢神経系への効率的な抗体デリバリーと持続的な発現を可能にする本技術は、免疫活性化が関与する慢性疼痛の新たな治療選択肢となる可能性があります。

title: Burn Injury Rewires Immune and Neuronal Extracellular Vesicle Communication.
abstract: Objective We examined extracellular vesicle (EV) protein alterations after burn injury to elucidate molecular pathways linking immune-neural communication and the pathophysiology of burns. Background Severe burn injury triggers widespread inflammation and metabolic stress with downstream consequences. EVs are essential mediators of cell-to-cell communication and protein transport for regulating inflammation, metabolism, and neuronal signaling that may reflect burn-related alterations. Methods Plasma EVs from 37 adult burn patients (≥15% total body surface area burn [TBSA]) and 21 nonburn controls were analyzed. An age-restricted subcohort ( Results Burn injury produced distinct alterations in EV proteomic profiles. Among 919 detected proteins, 326 were decreased and 593 were increased. The 5 most significant proteins (adjusted P -value Conclusions Burn injury profoundly alters EV cargo across general, immune, and neuronal types, reflecting proinflammatory and neuroimmune-associated signaling. This coordinated EV remodeling may reflect the hyperinflammatory responses, altered healing, and downstream biological pathway alterations. EV-based biomarkers may enable improved diagnostic and therapeutic strategies to mitigate dysregulated immune and healing responses in burn patients.
authors: Grimsrud KN, Green T, Tang Y, Clayton SM, Ward BM, Wang D, Durbin-Johnson B, Wang A, Palmieri TL.
screening_reason: The study investigates alterations in extracellular vesicles that reflect proinflammatory and neuroimmune-associated signaling after burn injury.
summary_ja: 熱傷患者37名と非熱傷対照群21名の血漿細胞外小胞（EV）のプロテオーム解析を行い、熱傷後の免疫・神経間コミュニケーションの変化を調査しました。熱傷によりEVのタンパク質プロファイルは著しく変化し、急性期反応、凝固系、および神経炎症に関連する経路の活性化が示されました。特に免疫細胞および神経由来のEVにおいて、炎症性および神経免疫関連のシグナル伝達を反映する協調的な変化が観察されました。このEVの再編成は、熱傷後の過剰な炎症反応や治癒プロセスの変化を反映している可能性があります。
summary_en: This study analyzed plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) from 37 burn patients and 21 controls to investigate immune-neural communication after burn injury. Burn injury significantly altered the EV proteomic profile, with enrichment in pathways related to acute phase response, coagulation, and neuroinflammation. These findings suggest that burn injury induces coordinated remodeling of immune- and neuron-derived EVs, reflecting systemic hyperinflammatory and neuroimmune responses.
key_finding_ja: 熱傷患者の血漿細胞外小胞（EV）プロテオームは著しく変化しており、急性期反応や神経炎症などの神経免疫関連シグナル伝達の変調が示されました。
why_it_matters_ja: 熱傷後の全身性炎症や神経免疫応答の病態解明に寄与し、新たな診断用バイオマーカーや治療標的の開発につながる可能性があります。

title: A multi-target nano-therapy against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury via combinatorial inhibition of neuroinflammation and pyroptosis.
abstract: Background & purpose : ischemic stroke reperfusion injury involves a vicious cycle of neuroinflammation, pyroptosis, and oxidative stress. Single-target therapies have limited efficacy. In this study, we aimed to develop an actively targeted, multi-drug combinatorial nano-platform for coordinated intervention against ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. Methods : we synthesized CX3CL1-functionalized ZIF-8 nanoparticles co-loaded with disulfiram (DFL, a GSDMD-N pore inhibitor), paquinimod (PAQ, a TLR4/NF-κB inhibitor), and siNINJ1 (inhibiting membrane rupture). The nanoparticles were systematically characterized. Their neuroprotective effects and mechanisms were evaluated using a transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) mouse model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) co-culture model in vitro . Results : the nanoparticles exhibited pH-responsive release and active targeting to the ischemic penumbra. In vivo and in vitro results demonstrated that they synergistically inhibited the TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling axis and pyroptosis execution (GSDMD, caspase-1), promoted microglial polarization towards the M2 phenotype, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α), and alleviated oxidative stress and neuronal apoptosis, ultimately leading to significantly reduced infarct volume and improved neurological recovery. Conclusion : we successfully developed an "active targeting-multi-drug synergy-cascade intervention" nano-therapeutic platform that effectively mitigates cerebral I/R injury through multi-pathway coordination, offering a novel combinatory strategy for ischemic stroke treatment.
authors: Fu W, Zhao A, Chen B, Feng Y, Shen H, Li J, Zeng X.
screening_reason: The paper evaluates a therapeutic strategy designed to inhibit neuroinflammation and microglial activation in cerebral ischemia.
summary_ja: 脳虚血再灌流障害に対処するため、ジスルフィラム、パキニモド、およびsiNINJ1を共担持した多標的指向型ナノ粒子プラットフォームが開発されました。マウスの一過性中大脳動脈閉塞モデルおよびin vitro共培養モデルにおいて、このナノ粒子は虚血ペナンブラを能動的に標的とし、pH応答性に薬剤を放出しました。このナノ治療は、TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3シグナル軸とパイロトーシス実行因子を相乗的に抑制し、ミクログリアのM2表現型への分極を促進しました。その結果、酸化ストレスや神経細胞アポトーシスが軽減され、脳梗塞体積の有意な減少と神経機能の回復が確認されました。
summary_en: Researchers developed a multi-target nanoparticle platform co-loaded with disulfiram, paquinimod, and siNINJ1 to target cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury. In mouse and in vitro models, these nanoparticles actively targeted the ischemic penumbra and synergistically inhibited neuroinflammation and pyroptosis pathways. The treatment promoted M2 microglial polarization, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and decreased infarct volume, leading to improved neurological recovery.
key_finding_ja: 開発された多標的ナノ粒子は、脳虚血再灌流モデルにおいて神経炎症とパイロトーシスを相乗的に抑制し、脳梗塞体積を減少させて神経機能を改善しました。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳卒中後の複雑な病態に対して複数の経路を同時に制御する新たな治療戦略となる可能性があり、今後の臨床応用への展開が期待されます。

title: Dose Titration of Plant-Based Flavonoid Blend Supplementation on Performance, Digestibility, Gut Microbiome, Blood Biomarkers, and Meat Quality of Growing Rabbits.
abstract: Rabbit meat is increasingly valued for its high nutritional quality, driving growing interest in enhancing its production through phytobiotics like plant-based flavonoid blend (PFB). So, this study looked at how a PFB at different doses influences the performance, digestibility, gut microbiota, blood biomarkers, liver health, and meat quality of growing rabbits. Sixty rabbits (body weight 552.63 ± 13.44 g) were assigned at random to five dietary groups, having twelve replicates per group. The rabbits were fed a basal diet as a total mixed ration having 17.02% crude protein and 11.60 MJ metabolizable energy/kg dry matter (DM), supplemented with PFB (g/kg diet) at 0.0 (control), 0.20, 0.40, 0.60, and 0.80. Following a 2 weeks adjustment period, the feeding trial was conducted for 5 weeks. When the trial was over, rabbits were sacrificed to collect digesta, blood, and meat samples for further analysis. Supplementation with PFB at 0.60 g/kg diet (range: 0.50-0.70 g/kg) showed a better final body weight ( p = 0.01), weight gain ( p p p p = 0.02) digestibility. Besides, supplementation with PFB presented a linear reduction in Escherichia coli ( p = 0.003), accompanied by linear improvement in Lactobacillus spp. ( p p = 0.001). Broken-line analysis indicated optimal PFB supplementation levels of 0.60, 0.47, and 0.60 g/kg diet for E. coli, Lactobacillus spp., and HDL-C, respectively. However, feed intake, serum triglycerides, other cholesterols, total protein, albumin, globulin, and uric acid remained unchanged across the groups. Furthermore, supplementation with PFB with an estimated breakpoint of 0.55 g PFB/kg of diet effectively ( p ≤ 0.02) reduced serum liver enzymes (aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, and alkaline phosphatase) indicating better liver health. In addition, PFB supplementation linearly reduced meat ether extract content and improved meat redness ( p < 0.001), with optimal responses at 0.58 and 0.60 g/kg diet, respectively, while having no impacts on meat protein, ash, lightness, or yellowness. Therefore, dietary inclusion of PFB at 0.55 g-0.60 g per kg diet optimized growth performance through enhanced weight gain, feed efficiency, and nutrient digestibility, while favorably modulating cecum microbiome, serum cholesterol, liver enzyme activities, and ameliorated meat quality.
authors: Rahman MA, Hasan MM, Hashem MA, Siddique MP, Chowdhury R.
screening_reason: The study evaluates the effects of dietary supplementation on the cecum gut microbiome and microbial composition in rabbits.
summary_ja: 成長期のウサギ60頭を対象に、植物由来フラボノイドブレンド（PFB）の添加量が成長、消化率、腸内細菌叢などに及ぼす影響を5週間の飼育試験で評価しました。PFBを0.55〜0.60 g/kgの割合で飼料に添加したところ、体重増加、飼料効率、および栄養素の消化率が最適化されました。また、PFBの添加は盲腸内の大腸菌を減少させ、乳酸菌（Lactobacillus spp.）を増加させるなど、腸内細菌叢を良好に調節しました。さらに、血清中の肝酵素活性の低下や肉質の改善も確認されました。
summary_en: This study evaluated the effects of different doses of a plant-based flavonoid blend (PFB) on growing rabbits over a five-week feeding trial. Supplementation with PFB, particularly at 0.55 to 0.60 g/kg, optimized growth performance, feed efficiency, and nutrient digestibility. Furthermore, PFB intake favorably modulated the cecal microbiome by reducing Escherichia coli and increasing Lactobacillus spp., while also improving liver health biomarkers and meat quality.
key_finding_ja: 成長期のウサギへの植物由来フラボノイドブレンド添加は、大腸菌の減少と乳酸菌の増加を伴う盲腸内細菌叢の改善や、成長パフォーマンスの向上をもたらしました。
why_it_matters_ja: 家畜の生産効率向上と腸内環境改善を両立する天然由来の飼料添加物として、畜産業における実用的な活用が期待されます。

title: Arbutin mediated neuroprotection in zebrafish model of traumatic brain injury via modulating Nrf2/NF-κB pathway.
abstract: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) is a major cause of mortality and disability worldwide and is associated with oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neurotransmitter imbalance. Arbutin, a naturally occurring glycoside with known antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, has the potential to modulate neurochemical alterations following brain injury. The present study was designed to evaluate the neuroprotective effects of arbutin in a zebrafish model of TBI induced by a novel non-invasive mechanical impact method termed "force-induced TBI." Adult zebrafish were randomly divided into seven groups (n = 14 per group): normal control, TBI control, arbutin per se, arbutin-treated groups (25, 50, and 100 mg/kg, i.p.), and a co-treatment group receiving arbutin (100 mg/kg) co-administrated with chrysin (25 mg/kg), a known modulator of the Nrf2/NF-κB signaling pathway. Behavioural assessments, including the open field test, novel tank diving test (NTDT), T-maze, and novel object recognition test (NORT), were conducted on days 1, 4, and 7 to evaluate locomotion activity, anxiety-like behaviour, spatial memory, and recognition ability, respectively. Following behavioural evaluation, brain tissues were analysed for oxidative stress markers (MDA, nitrite, GSH, and SOD), neurotransmitter levels (GABA and glutamate), pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6), and histopathological alterations. Immunohistochemical analysis of Nrf2 and NF-κB was also performed. The results demonstrated that arbutin significantly improved behavioural performance, restored oxidative balance, normalized neurotransmitter levels, and attenuated neuroinflammatory responses. Furthermore, arbutin treatment was associated with increased Nrf2 immunoreactivity and reduced NF-κB immunoreactivity in a dose-dependent manner. The co-treatment with chrysin also exhibited protective effects, supporting its potential modulatory role in oxidative stress and these effects are associated with modulation of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, neurotransmitter imbalance, and Nrf2/NF-κB immunoreactivity. These findings suggest that arbutin possesses neuroprotective potential against secondary brain injury and is associated with modulation of oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, and Nrf2/NF-κB immunoreactivity.
screening_reason: The study evaluates the attenuation of neuroinflammatory responses and microglial activation in a model of traumatic brain injury.
summary_ja: 本研究では、成体ゼブラフィッシュの新規「力学誘発性」外傷性脳損傷（TBI）モデルを用いて、アルブチンの神経保護効果を評価しました。アルブチン投与により、行動障害が有意に改善し、酸化ストレスのバランスが回復し、神経伝達物質レベルが正常化し、神経炎症反応が減弱しました。これらの効果は、Nrf2免疫活性の増加およびNF-κB免疫活性の低下と用量依存的に関連していました。また、Nrf2/NF-κB経路の修飾因子であるクリシンとの併用投与も保護効果を示し、アルブチンの作用機序を裏付けました。
summary_en: This study evaluated the neuroprotective effects of arbutin in a novel "force-induced" traumatic brain injury (TBI) model in adult zebrafish. Arbutin treatment significantly improved behavioral performance, restored oxidative balance, normalized neurotransmitter levels, and attenuated neuroinflammatory responses. These protective effects were associated with the dose-dependent upregulation of Nrf2 and downregulation of NF-κB immunoreactivity.
key_finding_ja: ゼブラフィッシュのTBIモデルにおいて、アルブチンがNrf2/NF-κB経路の変調を介して酸化ストレス、神経伝達物質の不均衡、および神経炎症を抑制し、行動および組織学的転帰を改善することを示しました。
why_it_matters_ja: 外傷性脳損傷後の二次的脳損傷に対する新規治療薬候補として、天然配糖体であるアルブチンの有用性やその分子標的が示唆されます。

title: Enzyme-treated soybean meal in diets for weanling pigs.
abstract: Objective The objective of the present contribution is to provide a summary of the nutritional value of enzyme-treated soybean meal (ESBM) and review effects of ESBM on growth performance of weanling pigs. Guidelines for inclusion rates of ESBM in diets for weanling pigs will also be provided based on the published literature. Methods The literature review was conducted in May 2024 by searching Google Scholar and PubMed for experiments in which ESBM was included in diets for weanling pigs, using Boolean queries implemented with Biopython/Entrez. A total of 24 unique papers were identified. These papers were manually reviewed by reading to verify their relevance to the specific topics of composition, digestibility, and health/performance outcomes. Results Enzyme-treated soybean meal contains 48.3% to 57.7% crude protein, is rich in amino acids, and has elevated small-peptide fractions. Anti-nutritional factors such as raffinose and stachyose were reduced by 50% and 90% , respectively, compared with conventional soybean meal (SBM), and trypsin inhibitors are reduced to 1.7 units per mg. Enzyme-treated SBM also contains more fiber, but less monosaccharides and oligosaccharides, than SBM. Enzyme-treated SBM was associated with fewer gastrointestinal disturbances, favorable changes in intestinal microbiota, and improved intestinal barrier indices. In most experiments, pigs fed ESBM had improved growth performance and less diarrhea compared with pigs fed diets containing conventional SBM. Most experiments that examined the nutritional value of ESBM concluded that ESBM supports improved nutrient utilization, growth performance, and health in weanling pigs and on average, inclusion rates of 4% to 10% is recommended. Conclusion Enzyme-treated SBM has greater concentration of protein and contains fewer anti-nutritional factors than conventional SBM, which results in greater intestinal health and improved growth performance of weanling pigs if the inclusion rate of ESBM is 4% to 10% in diets for newly weaned pigs.
screening_reason: The review evaluates the effects of enzyme-treated soybean meal on intestinal microbiota and gut health in pigs.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、離乳子豚における酵素処理大豆粕（ESBM）の栄養価と生理学的影響に関する文献をまとめたものです。ESBMは、従来の大豆粕と比較して粗タンパク質含有量が高く、ラフィノースやトリプシンインヒビターなどの抗栄養因子が大幅に低減されています。ESBMの給餌は、胃腸障害の減少、腸内細菌叢の好ましい変化、および腸管バリア指標の改善と関連していました。分析された文献に基づき、離乳直後の子豚の腸内健康と成長パフォーマンスを最適化するために、4%から10%の配合割合が推奨されています。
summary_en: This review synthesizes literature on the nutritional value and physiological effects of enzyme-treated soybean meal (ESBM) in weanling pigs. ESBM contains higher crude protein and significantly fewer anti-nutritional factors, such as raffinose and trypsin inhibitors, compared to conventional soybean meal. Dietary inclusion of ESBM is associated with reduced gastrointestinal disturbances, beneficial changes in the intestinal microbiota, and improved growth performance, with a recommended inclusion rate of 4% to 10%.
key_finding_ja: 酵素処理大豆粕は抗栄養因子が少なく、離乳子豚の腸内細菌叢の改善や腸管バリア機能の向上を介して、成長促進と下痢の減少に寄与することを示しました。
why_it_matters_ja: 離乳期の子豚における消化器系トラブルを軽減し、抗生物質に頼らない効率的な飼料設計を確立するための実用的なガイドラインとなる可能性があります。
